# roundupcancerlawyers.com

> roundupcancerlawyers.com is a legal resource by The Alvarez Law Firm, based in Coral Gables, Florida. The site provides information about Roundup cancer lawsuits — Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma, B-cell Lymphoma, Leukemia, Multiple Myeloma, and other glyphosate-linked blood cancers — with a focus on strict product liability claims against Monsanto and Bayer. Led by Alex Alvarez, Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer, and Herb Borroto, M.D., J.D., Medical-Legal Expert. The firm has recovered over $100 million from Big Tobacco using the same defective-product framework it applies to Roundup cases.

## Main Pages

- [roundupcancerlawyers.com — Home](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com): Roundup cancer lawsuits, our strict-liability edge, and how The Alvarez Law Firm holds Monsanto and Bayer accountable.

## Practice Areas & Case Information

- [Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma Roundup Lawsuit](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/non-hodgkin-lymphoma-lawsuit.html): The cancer most strongly tied to Roundup. Coverage of all NHL subtypes — DLBCL, Follicular, Marginal Zone, Mantle Cell, Burkitt, T-cell lymphomas, and more.
- [B-cell Lymphoma Roundup Lawsuit](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/b-cell-lymphoma-lawsuit.html): DLBCL, Follicular Lymphoma, Marginal Zone Lymphoma, Mantle Cell Lymphoma, Burkitt Lymphoma, Lymphoplasmacytic Lymphoma / Waldenstrom, SLL, and Hairy Cell Leukemia.
- [Leukemia & CLL Roundup Lawsuit](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/leukemia-lawsuit.html): Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia, Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma, and Hairy Cell Leukemia after glyphosate exposure.
- [Multiple Myeloma Roundup Lawsuit](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/multiple-myeloma-lawsuit.html): Plasma cell cancers in farmers, applicators, and other heavy-exposure workers.

## Blog — In-Depth Analysis

- [Roundup Cancer Lawsuit Insights — Blog Index](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/): All published analysis on Roundup litigation, glyphosate science, and case eligibility.
- [The Monsanto Papers Explained](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/monsanto-papers-explained.html): What internal Monsanto documents reveal about ghost-writing of "independent" science, attacks on the IARC classification, and EPA influence campaigns. Authored by Alex Alvarez.
- [Can I Still Sue Monsanto for Roundup in 2026?](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/can-i-still-sue-monsanto-roundup-2026.html): Yes. What Bayer's $10.9B settlement did and didn't resolve, why the federal MDL is still active, and how state-by-state statutes of limitations affect filing windows. Authored by Alex Alvarez.
- [IARC vs. EPA on Glyphosate: Why The Two Agencies Disagree](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/iarc-vs-epa-glyphosate.html): The WHO's IARC classifies glyphosate as Group 2A "probably carcinogenic." The EPA does not. Why the two agencies reached opposite conclusions and which is more persuasive in court. Authored by Herb Borroto, M.D., J.D.
- [Strict Liability vs. Failure-to-Warn: Why It Matters For Your Roundup Case](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/strict-liability-vs-failure-to-warn.html): Two roads to a defective-product verdict against Monsanto. Why strict product liability is harder for Monsanto to escape, and the tobacco-litigation precedent for using it. Authored by Alex Alvarez.
- [Who Qualifies for a Roundup Lawsuit: Farmers, Landscapers, Homeowners](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/who-qualifies-roundup-lawsuit.html): Three exposure categories (agricultural workers, landscapers and groundskeepers, residential users) and four qualifying cancer families. What we need to evaluate a case. Authored by Alex Alvarez, medical review by Herb Borroto, M.D., J.D.
- [Glyphosate Exposure for Landscapers and Groundskeepers — Occupational Roundup Claims](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/glyphosate-exposure-landscapers-groundskeepers.html): Professional landscapers and institutional groundskeepers had some of the highest documented occupational glyphosate exposure (daily application over years/decades, gallons per shift, direct skin contact, inhalation, documented application records). What makes their cases distinctive and the qualifying cancers (NHL, multiple myeloma, B-cell lymphoma, leukemia/CLL).
- [Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) and Roundup — Treatment and Case Strength](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/dlbcl-diffuse-large-b-cell-lymphoma-roundup.html): DLBCL is the most common NHL in the U.S. (~30% of NHL diagnoses) and one of the cancers most strongly linked to glyphosate exposure in the IARC and subsequent meta-analysis literature. R-CHOP first-line treatment, autologous stem cell transplant and CAR-T for relapsed/refractory disease, and the damages picture for surviving and deceased plaintiffs.
- [Roundup Bellwether Trial Results — What They Mean for New Cases](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/roundup-bellwether-trial-results-meaning.html): What bellwethers are and how they shape mass tort litigation; the Roundup bellwether record (Johnson 2018, Hardeman 2019, Pilliod 2019) establishing the basic causation framework, Monsanto's internal-document credibility problems, and the mixed-result pattern in subsequent trials; what the record means for case evaluation and settlement leverage today.
- [Farmworkers, Agricultural Workers, and Roundup — What's Different About Your Case](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/farmworkers-agricultural-workers-roundup-cases.html): The agricultural exposure profile (direct application, reentry exposure, container handling, equipment cleaning, drift); the NIH Agricultural Health Study and its role; what's different about farmworker cases (documentation, restricted use products, Worker Protection Standard 40 CFR Part 170 compliance, multi-defendant potential); practical considerations including Spanish-language consultations.
- [Roundup vs. Other Glyphosate Products — Cumulative Exposure and Case Strength](https://roundupcancerlawyers.com/blog/roundup-vs-other-glyphosate-products-cumulative-exposure.html): The post-2000 generic glyphosate market (Monsanto's patent expired 2000); how multi-product exposure histories are evaluated (Roundup-predominant cases, mixed-substantial cases, non-Roundup predominant cases); IARC classification of glyphosate generally (not Roundup specifically) preserving causation across products; apportionment in multi-defendant cases.

## What Makes The Firm Different

- Most Roundup lawyers run failure-to-warn claims. The Alvarez Law Firm leads with strict product liability — the theory that Roundup is unreasonably dangerous as designed, regardless of any warning. This is the same framework the firm has used to recover over $100 million from Big Tobacco.
- Alex Alvarez is a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer, certified by the National Board of Trial Advocacy — a distinction held by less than 1% of Florida attorneys.
- Herb Borroto holds both a medical degree (M.D.) and a law degree (J.D.). He personally reviews pathology, oncology charts, immunohistochemistry, and bone marrow biopsies for every Roundup case — a level of in-house medical expertise most firms cannot match.

## Reference Documents Used In Cases

- IARC Monograph Vol. 112 (2015) — Glyphosate classified as Group 2A "probably carcinogenic to humans"
- The "Monsanto Papers" — Internal Monsanto documents released through Roundup litigation
- Federal Roundup MDL 2741 (Northern District of California)
- Agricultural Health Study and other peer-reviewed cohort and case-control studies

## Sources Cited On Site

Each page on this site carries a "Sources" section at the bottom citing primary sources (IARC, EPA, NIH/NCI, U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, American Cancer Society, peer-reviewed PubMed-indexed studies). The Alvarez Law Firm relies on government, academic, and peer-reviewed publications — not commercial summaries — for all factual claims about glyphosate, Roundup, and the linked blood cancers.
